jobs.description: Careers at Salesforce Skip to Content Careers at Salesforce Where Possibility Multiplies Welcome to our careers blog, your go-to place for exploring Salesforce and who we are. Here, you’ll find employee stories in their own words, an inside look at our culture, and answers to your most common Salesforce questions. Whether you’re just browsing or ready to apply, we’re so glad you’re here. Most Popular Blogs Dani Laven From mental health to family care to financial wellness, Salesforce benefits are designed to support every part of your life. Dani Laven For a long time, AI felt like someone else’s job. A developer’s job. A data scientist’s job. Not yours. That’s changed. Salesforce recruiters are looking for AI fluency across every role and the skills at the top of their list might surprise you. Preparing for an interview at the #1 AI CRM? Read how Teddy Sergesketter uses Salesforce’s volunteer time off to build community impact. Salesforce Careers Dani Laven • Senior Manager, Employer Brand Marketing Tyler Ng • Corporate Communications Intern Here’s to the Builders and Learners. The most powerful thing about Salesforce? Our people don’t wait to be told what’s next — they build it. Whether they’re shipping AI agents with Agentforce, earning Trailhead certifications on their lunch break, or mentoring the next generation of technologists, our builders and learners are what keep us at the cutting edge. Career growth here isn’t a ladder — it’s a lattice. We invest in curiosity, celebrate progress at every level, and make sure the tools to grow are always within reach. At Salesforce, we prioritize collaboration over ego, innovation over process, and learning over perfection. Our culture is fast-moving and team-first, where everyone’s voice is heard and valued. We believe in the power of collective intelligence and the importance of continual improvement. What are the compensation and benefits like for tech and product roles? We offer highly competitive pay, equity, world-class benefits, and performance-based reward

jobs.title: AI fluency is increasingly important across Salesforce
jobs.description: Salesforce AI Skills for Every Candidate Skip to Content 0% Share article AI isn’t just changing tech jobs — it’s changing every job. Most professionals are somewhere in the middle of figuring out what that means for them in their careers, and that’s exactly who this blog is for. We sat down with Salesforce recruiters to answer the questions coming up most across every function right now. Turns out, being ready looks a lot less like coding and a lot more like curiosity, adaptability, and knowing where to grow. Read on to learn what AI fluency actually looks like, what hiring teams are paying attention to right now, and how to demonstrate it. What do Salesforce recruiters look for? We evaluate more than a résumé. We’re looking for high-velocity learners who bring genuine curiosity, adapt quickly, and invest in their own growth. The trajectory matters as much as the track record. AI fluency is one of the clearest signals of that. It’s a core competency we evaluate across every role, just in different ways. Technical candidates may complete an assessment demonstrating how they use AI. Non-technical candidates should be ready to talk about their toolkit and what they’ve learned from it. No matter the role, come with a point of view on working alongside AI and a curiosity to keep evolving. The best way to demonstrate that mindset? Trailhead . Our free, on-demand learning platform gives everyone access to the training and certifications needed to thrive in the agentic enterprise. Whether you’re looking to pivot your career, deepen your expertise, or just try something new, Trailhead has everything you need to set yourself apart. So, what is Trailhead — and is it really free? Yes, completely. Trailhead is Salesforce’s free, on-demand learning platform: no CRM account, no paywalls, no prerequisites. It’s built for every role and experience level, from someone exploring AI for the first time to a seasoned developer looking to go deeper. With a website and mobile app (iOS and Android), you can learn wherever you are. Artificial Intelligence Fundamentals Learn the basics of AI and the tech behind its amazing capabilities. Visit Trail +100 points Trail Get Started with AI What does AI fluency actually mean? Think of AI fluency the same way you’d think about any professional skill: it’s about knowing how to use the right tool at the right time. For most roles, that has nothing to do with writing code. Our AI Fluency Playbook is a great starting point, followed by these Trailhead modules: Artificial Intelligence Fundamentals : Understand how agentic AI works and where it fits in the modern workplace. (~10 min) Responsible Creation of Artificial Intelligence : Build the ethical judgment that defines a thoughtful AI practitioner. (~45 min) Prompt Fundamentals : Learn how to communicate clearly with AI tools to get better, faster results. (~25 min) Curious about where AI can take your career? Explore the 10 New Jobs Created by AI and See if One Is Right for You. How do I demonstrate AI skills on my résumé? Fewer buzzwords, more evidence. “Familiar with AI tools” doesn’t tell us much; specifics do. Here’s what stands out: Certifications and badges : If you’ve earned them, list them. Trailhead certifications are verifiable, credible, and signal that you’ve done the work, not just read about it. Agentblazer Status: Your Agentblazer level tells us you’ve invested energy in understanding agentic AI specifically, which is exactly where the industry is headed. Specific outcomes: “Used AI to reduce report prep time by X hours a week” is far more compelling than “leveraged AI tools to improve efficiency.” Show impact, not just activity. A learning trail: We love seeing progression. Someone who earned three badges last quarter and two certifications this quarter is showing us something important: that they don’t stop growing. Trailhead profile link: Add it. Seriously. It’s a living résumé that updates every time you complete something new. The through line across all of it is the same thing we look for in every candidate: intentionality. We want to see that you made a choice to grow, and that you can tell us exactly what you gained from it. How do I showcase AI fluency in the interview? The interview is your chance to show us how you think with AI, not just that you use it. There’s a difference between tactical use (“I had AI write my recap email”) and strategic use (“I used AI to pressure-test my proposal before presenting to leadership”). Walk us through a real example — personal or professional — where you pushed AI beyond the surface level. Bonus points for telling us what you tried, what didn’t work, and how you adjusted. That kind of reflection is exactly what AI fluency looks like in practice. AI Fluency Playbook As we build the Agentic Enterprise, leaders must enable employees to understand, apply, and redesign work to succeed in the human + agent workforce. Learn more Is AI required at Salesforce — and how does the team actually use it? Technical AI skills vary by role, but working alongside AI is universal. Agentforce and Slackbot are embedded into how we operate across every function including roles in Sales, Marketing, HR, and Finance. You don’t necessarily need to know how to build it, but you do need a genuine openness to grow alongside the technology that’s reshaping how work gets done. I don’t really know about AI. Is it too late to start learning? Not even close. We’re at the very beginning of the agentic era, and the tools, roles, and possibilities are still being defined. The people who start now are the ones who will help shape what comes next. Wherever you are, the right moment to start is now. Here are some of the best places to begin: Get Started with Artificial Intelligence : Learn how artificial intelligence works and how to use it effectively and responsibly. jobs.title: how we hire
jobs.description: How We Hire at Salesforce | Interviewing at Salesforce | Salesforce Skip to content Search jobs Join our Talent Community Search jobs Explore Agentforce Explore Learn Apply Interview Learn more Search jobs Can I apply to multiple jobs? We love that ambition, Trailblazer! And yes — you absolutely can. That said, for the best candidate experience, we recommend applying to no more than three roles within a 12-month period. This gives our recruiting team more time to dedicate to each application and helps you focus on the jobs that are best matched to, well, you. Do I need a technical background to work at Salesforce? Nope! We have all kinds of opportunities across a variety of teams and business functions at Salesforce, including non-technical roles. (Hey, someone’s writing these FAQs!) We’re focused on hiring high-performing talent who can help drive the company forward. The most important thing you can do is make sure that your skills and qualifications on your resume match those outlined in the job posting. Will my interview(s) take place virtually or in person? Throughout the interview process, most conversations will take place in a virtual setting over Google Meet. Candidates are expected to be on camera during each virtual interview per Salesforce hiring policies. If you are unable to be on camera throughout the interview process, please submit an accommodation request . In addition, an on-site interview at a Salesforce office will be required prior to receiving an offer. Your recruiter will provide more details throughout the hiring process. How can I prepare for an interview? Preparation is key to showing off your best, most confident self! First, we recommend you carefully review the job description, and get ready to demonstrate how your skills and experiences tie back to the qualifications for the role. Our hiring teams want to hear about real-life situations and may ask questions that are behavioral, competency-based, or situational. We also encourage you to have a foundational understanding of our business. (Pssst: Get started by learning about us on Trailhead , our gamified learning platform.) What if I need an accommodation for my interview? We’re happy to help! Send a request via our Accommodation Request Form for assistance and/or an accommodation due to a disability during the application or recruiting process. What types of benefits will I receive as a Salesforce employee? We care about you (yes, you!) thriving inside and outside of work, and we offer world-class benefits for our employees and their loved ones around the globe. And great news — you can get a sneak peek of our benefits right now via our Benefits Site . We aim to prioritize the resources and tools that matter most to our employees — from top-tier benefits to wellbeing resources — because we only succeed when you succeed. What if I left recently — should I wait before applying? Not at all. If you’re ready to return, we’re ready to talk — no waiting required. We value your experience and the unique perspective you bring, and we’re excited to reconnect with you. Apply today Join our Talent Community

jobs.description: Salesforce Volunteering: Employee Programs, VTO, and Giving | Salesforce Skip to content Start here What is Salesforce's volunteer time off (VTO) program? Salesforce's VTO program provides employees with seven paid days (56 hours) of time off each year to dedicate to volunteering. How many hours have Salesforce employees volunteered? In 2025, Salesforce surpassed 10 million all-time volunteer hours. You can find our latest volunteer hour milestone here . How do employees use their volunteer time off (VTO)? Employees are encouraged to use their VTO in ways that are personal to them, such as volunteering at a school, virtual mentoring, or supporting organizations with technical and professional expertise. Does Salesforce offer a matching gift program for giving? Yes, employees can maximize their impact through up to USD $10,000 in matching gifts annually, and they are also eligible for special grant programs tied to volunteering milestones. What are the benefits of Salesforce volunteering for employees? Employees who participate in volunteering and giving programs report feeling more connected to Salesforce culture (77%) and having a deeper sense of meaning and purpose (88%).
